blockers: required workload pending: mission.inventory.full — No pinned upstream command emits the Rust inventory document. specify_cli.context.mission_resolver.list_missions_for_selection exposes only slug/mid8/friendly_name; comparing the full document would require reimplementing the Rust projection in the oracle. Tracked as mission.list.projection (diagnostic).

required workload pending: mission.show — No pinned upstream command emits the same per-mission WP summary. agent tasks list-tasks/status are lane-and-state views; using them would compare different work. The dependency edge subset is covered diagnostically by mission.graph.projection.

required workload pending: project.root — Upstream locates the project root internally (locate_project_root) but exposes no CLI contract for it. A comparison would be startup-class discovery, not a representative workload; it must not be used as gate evidence.

required workload pending: git.inspect — Upstream has Git helpers but no read-only inspection command with an equivalent document. ops log / safe-commit are different contracts. Needs a shared inspection contract before timing is meaningful.

required workload pending: mission.dependency_planning.full — Upstream planning surfaces (orchestrator-api mission-state, agent tasks status) reconstruct lanes/readiness; Rust mission graph is explicitly read-only and does not evaluate state. Outputs are not equivalent. Edge-only projection is diagnostic.

required workload pending: status.replay — Rust sk-status has no canonical reducer. events inspect states it is not a reducer. Upstream specify_cli.status.reducer.reduce / agent status materialize are the oracle, but no native counterpart exists yet.

required workload pending: runtime.next.governed — Rust runtime query is a pure planner over an explicit snapshot. Upstream next reads and writes a run store, resolves owned workspaces, emits prompt files, and applies gates; it is a different contract and must be implemented before it can be paired.

required workload pending: events.inspect — Rust events inspect is a Rust-specific typed projection (its category partition and torn-tail semantics have no upstream typed inspector). Python events tail is a line stream, not an equivalent contract. Must not be benchmarked as if equivalent.

required workload pending: governance.charter — No pinned upstream CLI emits the Rust charter.inspect document. Upstream charter status/context/validate are different contracts; activation/pack acquisition are mutating and unimplemented in Rust.

required workload pending: glossary.activation — Rust sk-glossary implements seed validation + lookup only. Upstream glossary event replay/extraction/middleware/activation mutations have no native counterpart.

required workload pending: lifecycle.mutations — Rust CLI is read-only: no project init, mission creation, lane/worktree ownership, event writes, acceptance, consolidation, merge, or recovery. These are the workloads that matter most for the final gate and must be native before they are benchmarked.
